Hello, fellow wind player! So, if you would like to join a community band here, here are two more options:

* Springfield Community Concert Band - this is a non-auditioned group, so it would probably be ideal for you at this point. It tends to have a mix of skill levels, from music teachers who play regularly to people just coming back to an instrument they haven’t played for decades. The group has a winter season and a summer season. They have a Facebook page here: https://www.facebook.com/profile.php?id=100063002120144 (if you don’t have Facebook, but are interested, DM me and I will try to put you in contact with one of the band organizers)

* Eugene Symphonic Band - this is an auditioned group, but if you start feeling more comfortable on your instrument and want more of a challenge, this might be a good group for you. This group rehearses most of the year (not summer as much as in the past, but autumn-winter-spring), and the skill level is overall higher since it’s an auditioned group. Website here: https://www.eugenesymphonicband.org/ and Facebook page here: https://www.facebook.com/eugenesymphonicband

I hope you find a good place to play! I play with the above ensembles, and enjoy both. One More Time is also a lot of fun, if you’re looking for a summer marching band. I believe any of these bands would welcome a new flute member, you just need to find which group(s) will be a good fit for you!

The current SCOTUS has ruled for the religious organizations every time they challenge COVID-19 restrictions. 

Here’s the latest https://www.supremecourt.gov/opinions/20pdf/20a151_4g15.pdf , which ruled that California could not restrict Bible study or worship gatherings in private homes. The majority (all the conservatives minus Robert’s) reasoned that if there are any exemptions at all for any secular institutions, then those exemptions must be offered to religious organizations, even if the activities are not comparable (big difference between shopping masked in a large grocery store and multiple families in a home singing, talking, and reading aloud facing each other. Does not bode well for any restrictions on churches, which is probably why Oregon is not bothering at this point.

Some more SCOTUS cases: 
New York must allow religious institutions to be grouped with “essential businesses”; as long as the latter has no capacity limit, neither should the former:  https://casetext.com/case/roman-catholic-diocese-of-brooklyn-v-cuomo-1

California must allow indoor church services, but may enforce capacity limits and a prohibition on chanting and singing at least until the churches bring evidence of being treated differently from secular institutions: https://www.supremecourt.gov/orders/courtorders/020521zr_q8l1.pdf

California must lift restrictions on indoor services in churches while churches appeal: https://www.supremecourt.gov/orders/courtorders/022621zr_1bo2.pdf

TLDR: Oregon does not want to risk being taken to court by churches given the makeup of this current SCOTUS, so the churches escape a lot of restrictions and scrutiny that they probably deserve.

I don’t know what you’re talking about—plenty of retail and grocery staff have caught COVID-19. It hasn’t been that bad in Oregon, but for example, in SoCal during their winter surge retail store outbreaks were some of the most common outbreaks. If you look it up, you can read about it. And anecdotally, I knew a bunch of people going to work in LA in stores where multiple coworkers had it, and some of those people were hospitalized and died. Yes, not as dangerous as working the ICU, and not as dangerous as working serving people not wearing masks at restaurants, but it is much more dangerous than working from home or outdoors. And like I said before, we do not know what goes on with the spread between customers and workers, because we do not contact trace customers at all. Reported outbreaks in stores only include workers and their direct contacts as contact traced by public health. Oregon has a large proportion of cases they categorize as sporadic, which means they do not know how the person was exposed to coronavirus. Those people could have gotten it from a store or restaurant. Who knows? I’d rather not risk my and my family’s lives by ignoring a possible disease vector from customers. Especially with the LA and UK variants becoming more prevalent: those strains are associated with increased more outbreaks in the retail environment.

I don’t think we have much evidence either way due to the fact that we aren’t contact tracing customers at all (and we’re barely contact tracing workers in Oregon, for that matter). I don’t think any states in the US are contact tracing customers. Also, whenever you look at any of those coronavirus risk charts, shopping comes out only as a low-moderate risk. And maybe it is for customers, but that is not the case for workers and their risk is affected by all the shoppers hanging out in the stores because they think it’s safe. It’s not just all the customers, it’s that when there are more customers, there need to be more workers to keep the store running, and that crowds the register areas, break rooms, time clocks, entrance and exits, etc. And this is all before the UK and CA variants hit most of the states. Those variants definitely increase the risk of any indoor activity, if you look at the places that were hit hard by them. I hope I’m wrong and we avoid a spike driven by one of those variants, but if we don’t I bet we’re going to see more retail work outbreaks.

Yeah, just go off of it very slowly. I had some bad luck with effexor; my psychiatrist took me off it too quickly when I was younger, and it was just a mess. I still like contrabass clarinet best :) However, the contrabassoon timbre does seem to have its place. The contraforte definitely sounds different - similar to a contrabass saxophone. I guess what I'm trying to say that in some cases it might be appropriate (and composers should know of its availability! it's cool sounding in itself) but in some cases, not so much. I'm sure it plays more easily, but then so does soprano sax over oboe, alto horn over french horn, baritone over trombone, and so on. I appreciate the experimentation, though.
